name: kitex-service
description: Complete Kitex (Thrift) service project: Nacos registration, logging, config, Makefile codegen, CI for GitHub Actions and/or GitLab CI, Dockerfile. Used by `devkit ngs`.

vars.name: Service
vars.description: Service name, lowercase with dashes (e.g. order, order-item)

vars.name: Module
vars.description: Go module path of the new service (e.g. github.com/sezznaw/order)

vars.name: CommonModule
vars.description: Module path of the shared common library. Decided by the template for every service; cannot be set per service or project

vars.name: CommonVersion
vars.description: Version of common to require. Decided by the template for every service; cannot be set per service or project

vars.name: IdlRepo
vars.description: Path of the shared IDL project as CI sees it (owner/repo on GitHub, group/project on GitLab). Empty: <owner or group of the service>/idl

vars.name: CI
vars.description: Which CI configuration to generate: github, gitlab, both or none. ngs detects it from module_prefix / idl_repo

vars.name: GoPrivate
vars.description: GOPRIVATE pattern when the organisation's modules are private (empty = public)

vars.name: Port
vars.description: Listen port. Decided by the project's port table (idl/ports.yaml): the gateway is 8080, every other service owns ten ports from 8100 on; devkit ngs assigns the next free block

vars.name: CallbacksPort
vars.description: Port of the callback listener (callbacks.addr). devkit sets it to Port + 1 from the project's port table

vars.name: NacosAddr
vars.description: Address of the Nacos on a developer's own machine, written to conf/local.yaml

vars.name: GoVersion
vars.description: Go release (major.minor) for go.mod, the Docker image and GitLab CI; must not be lower than what devkit-common requires. Decided by the template for every service; cannot be set per service or project

vars.name: KitexVersion
vars.description: Kitex library and tool version. Decided by the template for every service; cannot be set per service or project

vars.name: ThriftgoVersion
vars.description: thriftgo tool version. Decided by the template for every service; cannot be set per service or project

vars.name: ValidatorVersion
vars.description: Version of thrift-gen-validator (IsValid from the IDL's vt.* annotations). Decided by the template

vars.name: DevkitVersion
vars.description: devkit version `make lint` runs (go run github.com/sezznaw/devkit@<version> lint). Decided by the template for every service

vars.name: LocalMySQLDB
vars.description: Database of the local stack, written as the default of conf/local.yaml's mysql.db

vars.name: LocalMySQLUser
vars.description: User of the local stack's database (conf/local.yaml default)

vars.name: LocalMySQLPassword
vars.description: Password of the local stack's database (conf/local.yaml default; a laptop value, never a real secret)

vars.name: LocalMySQLRootPassword
vars.description: Root password of the local stack's MySQL, for the test databases testx creates (Makefile default of MYSQL_TEST_DSN_ROOT; a laptop value)

vars.name: MigrationsDir
vars.description: Where the project's *.up.sql migrations are, relative to the service (Makefile default of MIGRATIONS_DIR, which testx.WithMySQL applies to a test database)

post_install: if command -v kitex >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v thriftgo >/dev/null 2>&1; then make gen && go mod tidy; else echo '>> kitex/thriftgo not installed. Run: make tools && make gen && go mod tidy'; fi
post_update: go get github.com/cloudwego/kitex@v0.16.3 github.com/sezznaw/devkit-common@v0.40.0 && if grep -rqs --include='*.go' --exclude-dir=kitex_gen 'github.com/sezznaw/devkit-common/log"' .; then echo '>> This service still imports devkit-common/log, which devkit-common v0.3.0 replaced by zlog.'; echo '>> go mod tidy was skipped, it cannot succeed until that code is changed.'; echo '>> Change it as described below, then run: go mod tidy'; else go mod tidy; fi

changes: devkit-common v0.40.0: overload protection of an RPC service (`limits:` section: max_in_flight 1000, max_qps off, max_connections 10000; refused requests get code 5003). devkit v0.9.11: lint flags server.WithLimit.

devkit-common v0.39.0: unique numbers. rt.ID.Next() is a 53-bit, time-ordered id unique across replicas (instance number leased in Redis), exact as a JSON / JavaScript number, so gateway IDLs keep i64; `id.instance_bits` (default 5) splits replicas against ids per millisecond. devkit v0.9.10.
CI: the build stage keeps .idl/ as an artifact, so the test stage's make lint runs the IDL rules (they were skipped in CI before).

devkit-common v0.37.1: tests. testx.New builds the Runtime on in-process Redis and Kafka, a recording Centrifugo and a MySQL database from the project's migrations (WithMySQL(testx.MigrationsDir())); make test passes MYSQL_TEST_DSN_ROOT (the local stack, skipped when absent) and MIGRATIONS_DIR; a sample test in handler/ (yours, created once). devkit v0.9.8: lint rule tests (a handler package needs a test).
devkit-common v0.36.0 (the gateway guard; nothing changes for an RPC service), devkit v0.9.7.

devkit-common v0.35.0: redisx.WithLock (a lock across replicas, auto-extended, Wait) and redisx.NewCache[T] (read-through cache with singleflight and negative caching); keys namespaced by the service. devkit v0.9.6: lint rules lock (hand-rolled SetNX) and mutex (sync.Mutex in handler/ or repo/).
devkit-common v0.34.2: the delayed-task gauges refresh every 15s instead of every poll (quieter SQL log).
devkit-common v0.34.1: the post-deploy `delay` check runs for every service with MySQL and skips one without the delayed_task table.

devkit-common v0.34.0: delayed tasks. rt.Delay.Schedule(ctx, tx, kind, key, at, payload) in the business transaction, rt.Delay.Handle(kind, fn) in app.Setup; at-least-once with backoff, failed state, metrics and the post-deploy `delay` check (table delayed_task from the migrations; `delay:` section in conf). devkit v0.9.5: lint rule delay (no time.AfterFunc / time.NewTimer in service code).
devkit v0.9.4: the money / rate lint rules match whole words of a field name (duration_ms, feedback no longer flagged).
devkit-common v0.33.0: hertzx.Audit, the back office's audit log from the IDL (// @audit, permission points), with an AsyncSink; apidoc writes x-audit.
devkit-common v0.32.1: the post-deploy gateway ping check retries while the Service's endpoints switch to the new pods.
app/verify.go renders (a `{{` in the Go code was read as a template action).

devkit-common v0.32.0: post-deploy verification. app/verify.go (yours, created once) lists the service's checks; main.go understands `--verify` (the framework's checks for mysql / redis / outbox / nacos / gateway ping, then yours, against the live deployment; exit 1 on failure); the deployment runs it as an ArgoCD PostSync Job after every release (chart `verify.enabled`), `make verify` runs it on your machine.
action: An existing service has no app/verify.go yet, and the new main.go needs it: copy app/verify.go from a new service (`devkit ngs` into a scratch directory) or from the template, then `go mod tidy`; then set `verify.enabled: true` in the service's infra values.

changes: devkit-common v0.31.1: a business code answered by a server middleware (validation 1001, idempotency 1002/1003/5002) now reaches the caller as a business error, not as 5001.

Request validation from the IDL: `make gen` runs thrift-gen-validator (vt.* annotations give every request an IsValid) and the framework's ValidationMiddleware (devkit-common v0.31.0) answers 1001 with the field and the rule before the handler runs. `make tools` installs the plugin.
action: Run `make tools` once (thrift-gen-validator), then `make gen`.

changes: devkit-common v0.30.0: the outbox. rt.Kafka.PublishTx(ctx, tx, ...) writes an event in the change's transaction; a relay publishes it (automatic with kafka + mysql; `kafka.outbox` section). devkit v0.9.2: lint rule outbox (no direct Publish next to a transaction).

devkit-common v0.29.0: moneyx is a decimal money (shopspring/decimal) in the currency's major unit, string amount in IDL and JSON, explicit rounding mode; rates are common.Decimal. devkit v0.9.1: lint rules money-type / rate-type / no-float-money for the decimal forms.

devkit-common v0.28.0: moneyx, the one representation of money (integer in the smallest unit plus a currency code; the IDL side is common.Money from idl/common/common.thrift). devkit v0.9.0: lint rule money-type refuses an IDL money field of any other type.
devkit-common v0.27.1: authx.HashPassword / VerifyPasswordHash / CheckPasswordPolicy (argon2id) for every account service; no service code needs to change.
devkit-common v0.27.0 (permission points for gateways; nothing changes for an RPC service).

devkit-common v0.26.2: a Centrifugo connection token subscribes its holder to the user's own channel server side (JWT `channels` claim), so a browser or app client needs no subscribe permission and cannot pick another user's channel; rt.Centrifugo.UserChannel(uid) names that channel; `centrifugo.user_channel` setting (default "user:").
devkit-common v0.26.0 (cors for API services; nothing changes for an RPC service).
devkit-common v0.25.1: apidoc takes only the first sentence of a method comment as the docs summary and drops directive lines (`// @public`) from the description; nothing else changes.
devkit-common v0.25.0: login state. conf gains an `auth:` section (off; only the authentication service turns it on). Handlers read the logged-in member with kitexx.UID(ctx).
action: conf/*.yaml are yours: add the `auth:` section (copy from a new service); a gateway also needs redis.enabled.

changes: devkit 0.7.0: the project-specific lint rules (vendor service, money words, error-code table) come from the IDL repository's devkit.yaml; the generic rules need no configuration. conf/local.yaml's database defaults come from the project's devkit.yaml vars (LocalMySQLDB / LocalMySQLUser / LocalMySQLPassword) instead of a fixed name.
devkit 0.6.2: idl-lock only asks for make gen when this service's own IDL directory changed, not on every IDL commit.
devkit 0.6.1: the idl-lock rule does not ask a shallow CI clone whether the IDL commit is pushed.

`make gen` writes idl.lock (the IDL commit the code was generated from) and CI builds against exactly that commit; a lock that lags the IDL checkout or an IDL commit not yet pushed fails `make lint` on your machine instead of the pipeline. Commit idl.lock with the service.
action: Run `make gen` once and commit the new idl.lock.

changes: `make lint` now also runs `devkit lint` (via go run, nothing to install): the team's rules from idl/AGENTS.md checked on your machine and in CI's test stage; a finding fails the pipeline. A line opts out with //devkit:lint-ignore <rule>.
devkit-common v0.24.0: the `version` of every record and span is APP_VERSION when log.version is empty; the deployment sets it to the image tag, so it no longer reads `-dirty` from CI builds.

devkit-common v0.23.0: `${VAR:-default}` in conf files. conf/local.yaml now carries the local stack's values as defaults (Nacos nacos/nacos, MySQL tenant_a, Centrifugo on 8000, ...), so `make run` needs no exports; a set variable still wins.
action: conf/local.yaml is yours: change `${NACOS_USERNAME}` to `${NACOS_USERNAME:-nacos}`, `${NACOS_PASSWORD}` to `${NACOS_PASSWORD:-nacos}`, and give the other local values defaults the same way (see a new service's local.yaml).

changes: devkit-common v0.22.1 (nothing changes for an RPC service).
devkit-common v0.22.0 (nothing changes for an RPC service).
devkit-common v0.21.2 (nothing changes for an RPC service).
devkit-common v0.21.0 (nothing changes for an RPC service).

devkit-common v0.20.0: every call to another service now has a 3s timeout, 1s connect timeout, one retry when the request was never sent, and a circuit breaker per service and method (kitexx.ClientOptions). New optional `rpc_client:` section to change them. The unused etcdx package was removed.

devkit-common v0.19.0: object storage. The conf files gain an `s3:` section (off); with s3.enabled the framework opens the bucket (source platform: the deployment's datasource row of kind s3) and rt.S3 gives Put / Get / Stat / List / Delete and presigned download and upload URLs, every file under this service's own prefix.
action: conf/*.yaml are yours: add the `s3:` section (enabled: false) to each; copy it from a new service or the template.

changes: Ports come from the project's port table (idl/ports.yaml, written by devkit ngs 0.3.0): every service owns a block of ten from 8100 on, +0 RPC, +1 the callback listener (callbacks.addr is now Port + 1), the rest reserved; the same port in every environment and in the deployment's values. Existing services keep their ports until their table entry says otherwise.

devkit-common v0.18.0: a Kitex service can receive provider callbacks. New `callbacks:` section in conf/*.yaml (off; the vendor-integration service turns it on, port 8081); in app.Setup `webhookx.Server(rt)` returns the HTTP engine and `webhookx.Handle` registers the routes; the listener starts and stops with the RPC server and the deployment exposes only it under /callbacks/.

devkit-common v0.17.0: provider callbacks. A provider's `callback:` entry (verify: hmac-sha256 / basic / custom, allow_cidrs, event_id, dedupe_ttl, archive_topic) and, in a Hertz service in the provider namespace, `webhookx.Handle(rt, h, '<provider>', '/callbacks/...', handler)` in app.Setup: source check, signature check, raw copy to Kafka, event-id dedupe through Redis, 500 on a handler error so the provider retries, metrics. Callback paths are the vendor's and are not in the IDL.
conf/*.yaml comments: the English and Chinese notes on provider secrets are separated by an empty line, as everywhere else.

devkit-common v0.16.0: provider authentication is configuration. `auth:` under a provider: bearer, basic, hmac-sha256 (payload template, timestamp header), oauth2 (client credentials, token cached and refreshed), or custom with a Signer your package provides (rt.Provider(name).UseSigner(...) in app.Setup). Secrets are ${ENV} values; the deployment injects the provider-secrets Secret into every service (variables named <PROVIDER>_<FIELD>).

devkit-common v0.15.0: a provider that is failing no longer slows the service down. Each provider has a circuit breaker (breaker_failures, default 5 consecutive failures; breaker_open_for, default 30s: calls fail at once with httpx.ErrCircuitOpen, then one probe) and a cap on calls in flight (max_concurrent, default 64). The connection pool keeps 100 idle connections per host. `debug: true` on a provider logs full requests and responses on your machine only.

devkit-common v0.14.0: external HTTP APIs. List them under `providers:` in conf/<env>.yaml (base_url, timeout, retries, headers from the environment) and take the client in app.Setup with rt.Provider('<name>'): GetJSON / PostJSON, or R() for anything resty does. Every call carries the trace, is one log record without secrets, and is counted (http_client_*). Retries only for idempotent methods on network errors, 429 and 5xx; a POST is never retried. A service with providers must be deployed to the -provider namespace; the framework refuses to start elsewhere.
action: conf/*.yaml are yours: add `providers: {}` (or your providers) to each; without the section nothing changes.

changes: devkit-common v0.13.0: Prometheus metrics. With `metrics.enabled` (new section in conf/*.yaml; on in dev/uat/prod, off in local) the framework serves /metrics on port 9091: requests per method with result code and latency histograms, calls to other services, MySQL pool, Redis commands, Kafka events, Go runtime. The deployment scrapes it and Grafana has a dashboard per service. Nothing to write.
action: conf/*.yaml are yours: add the `metrics:` section (enabled: true, addr: 9091 in dev/uat/prod; enabled: false in local). Without it metrics stay off.

changes: devkit-common v0.12.2: `--job=<name>` with a name the binary does not have logs an ERROR ("job not found; nothing run") before exiting 1.
devkit-common v0.12.1: a job run with tracing off logs its run id as trace_id instead of zeros.

devkit-common v0.12.0: scheduled jobs. app/jobs.go (yours, created once) lists the jobs: a name, a cron schedule in UTC, a timeout and a function. main.go understands `--list-jobs` (the CI stores the list next to the image tag and the deployment makes a Kubernetes CronJob of each job) and `--job=<name>` (what the CronJob runs: the framework opens what the configuration enables, runs the job with a root span, a run_id in the log, a Redis lock against overlap and the timeout, and exits 1 on failure; no server, no Nacos registration). `make jobs` lists them, `make job NAME=<name>` runs one on your machine.
action: An existing service has no app/jobs.go yet, and the new main.go needs it: copy app/jobs.go from a new service (`devkit ngs` into a scratch directory) or from the template, and `go mod tidy`. With an empty list nothing is scheduled; the CI still writes an empty jobs file.

changes: devkit-common v0.11.0: events and push. kafka.enabled gives rt.Kafka (Publish with the standard envelope and the trace; Subscribe in app.Setup, consumers run by rt.Run once the server is up, failures retried then parked in <topic>.dlq); centrifugo.enabled gives rt.Centrifugo (Publish to a channel, ConnectionToken). main.go now ends with rt.Run(svr). The conf files gain kafka: and centrifugo: sections, off by default.

devkit-common v0.10.0: Redis the way MySQL is done (redis.enabled in conf/<env>.yaml, source platform or static, rt.Redis, repo.Redis()), and idempotent requests: a Req with a request_id field is retried safely by the framework (same id = kept result, 1002 while running, 1003 empty id, 5002 without Redis). The conf files gain a `redis:` section, off by default.

devkit-common v0.9.0: MySQL opened by the framework. main.go now builds a kitexx.Runtime (logger, tracing, and what the configuration enables) and passes it to app.Setup(cfg, rt); a new package repo/ (yours, created once) holds the database code and gets rt.DB; handler.New takes the repo. Turn MySQL on with mysql.enabled in conf/<env>.yaml: source platform in deployments (the tenant's database from the platform's datasource table, TENANT_CODE from the deployment), source static on your machine. Every query is a span of the request's trace and a log record with its trace_id.

BREAKING for an existing service: after `devkit update` change app.Setup to `func Setup(cfg *Config, rt *kitexx.Runtime)`, add the repo/ package (copy repo/repo.go from a new service or from the template), and make handler.New take *repo.Repo. The conf files gain a `mysql:` section, off by default.

devkit-common v0.8.0: OpenTelemetry tracing. With `otel.endpoint` set (the deployment sets OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, e.g. Tempo on port 4317) every RPC is a server span, every call to another service a client span, and the W3C traceparent travels in the TTHeader, so Grafana shows the whole chain as a waterfall; the trace_id in the log is the id of that trace, so Loki and Tempo link to each other. Empty endpoint: nothing changes.
conf/*.yaml gain an `otel:` section (endpoint, sample_ratio). An existing service keeps working without it (tracing off); add the section to switch it on.

devkit-common v0.7.0, the version that API services created with `devkit nas` are built on. A project has one common/ for all its services, so RPC and API services move to a new common together. Nothing changes for an RPC service

devkit-common v0.6.1: shorter console lines. Records of the framework used to start with an absolute path, because the common library (common/ next to the service) and Kitex (the module cache) are outside the service's directory, and the message ended up off the screen. Now it is `common/kitexx/kitexx.go:185` and `github.com/cloudwego/kitex@v0.16.3/pkg/remote/remotesvr/server.go:79`. Your own code stays `handler/handler.go:32`; JSON logs are unchanged

devkit-common v0.6.0: every service logs which services are alive. At start one record, "services alive", lists every service with its number of instances and their addresses. After that "service online", "service offline" and "service instances changed" say what came or went and, again, everything that is alive, so when ser-auth starts, ser-user says so and shows the whole picture. It also sees the last instance of a service go, which the Nacos client that calls go through never hears of

with these records on, "service discovered" and "instances changed" of the services this one calls repeat them and move to debug; the warning that nothing can take the requests of a called service stays
action:
Nothing has to change: the records are on. To turn them off in one environment, add to the nacos section of that conf/*.yaml:
  watch_services: false

changes: a service whose name begins with "new" (news, new-order) compiles. thriftgo renames a Thrift service that begins with "New", because it would clash with the NewXxx constructors it generates: NewsService becomes package newsservice_. main.go imported newsservice, so such a service did not build after `devkit ngs`. main.go now follows that rule and refers to the package by a fixed alias

a start-up problem is logged from the step that failed. main.go called zlog.Fatal through a helper at the end of the file, so every "cannot start" record pointed at the same line of that helper, whether the configuration, the framework or app.Setup had failed. The helper is gone and the record names the line of the step

English and Chinese no longer run into each other. conf/README.md is English only and conf/README.zh-CN.md is the same document in Chinese, with a link to switch at the top of each; before, both languages shared lines, tables and YAML comments and neither could be read

new services get conf/*.yaml whose comments keep the languages apart: the English block, an empty comment line, then the Chinese block, and a file header that is English first and Chinese second. Nothing about the settings changed
action: Your conf/*.yaml are yours and keep their comments as they are. If you want the new layout, the quickest way is to generate a throwaway service with `devkit ngs` and copy the comments over; the settings are the same.

changes: four environments, one file each: conf/local.yaml (your own machine; what a service uses when APP_ENV is not set), conf/dev.yaml (the shared development server), conf/uat.yaml and conf/prod.yaml. "dev" used to mean the laptop, which left no name for the development server. `make run` uses local; the Docker image contains every environment except local

every environment uses Nacos, the laptop too: new services get a conf/local.yaml that registers in the Nacos on 127.0.0.1:8848 and refuses to start when it is not running. The file has the docker command, and reads the account from NACOS_USERNAME and NACOS_PASSWORD

devkit-common v0.5.0: a laptop never registers in a Nacos that other people use. In the local environment a service registers in a Nacos on the same machine only; anything else is refused at start. `nacos.register: false` is the way to work from your machine against the development server's Nacos: the service finds the others and reads its configuration there, and is not announced

devkit-common v0.5.0: what gets registered is the address this machine reaches Nacos from (the right one with a VPN or Docker networks; 127.0.0.1 with a local Nacos). `service.advertise` ("host" or "host:port", from ADVERTISE_ADDR in the deployed files) is registered instead, for containers that are reached through the host's address and a mapped port
action:
The default environment is now local, so a service without conf/local.yaml no longer starts on your machine. Your old conf/dev.yaml was the laptop file; make it that again, and give the servers theirs:
git mv conf/dev.yaml conf/local.yaml
cp conf/prod.yaml conf/dev.yaml     # then set   level: debug
cp conf/prod.yaml conf/uat.yaml

In conf/local.yaml set `registry_disabled: false` and the account of your Nacos (conf/README.md has every setting):
nacos:
  addrs: ["127.0.0.1:8848"]
  username: "${NACOS_USERNAME}"
  password: "${NACOS_PASSWORD}"

In conf/dev.yaml, conf/uat.yaml and conf/prod.yaml add below `addr:` (only matters for containers behind a mapped port):
  advertise: "${ADVERTISE_ADDR}"

changes: devkit-common v0.4.0: configuration that follows Nacos while the service runs. `kitexx.WatchConfig[Dynamic](cfg.Config)` reads the Nacos configuration `<service.name>.yaml` (setting `config_data_id`) into a struct and keeps it current: `Get()` is always the version in effect. A change that does not parse or validate is rejected and the previous version stays; the log lists what changed key by key, with secrets hidden, and points out keys with a typo. conf/README.md has a new section on it

registration and discovery are on record: `registered in Nacos`, `service discovered` and `instances changed` with a line per instance (`+ 10.0.0.7:8888  weight=10`, `- 10.0.0.6:8888`), `deregistered from Nacos`

the Nacos client logs through the logger of the service (`logger=nacos-sdk`, new setting `nacos.sdk_log_level`, default warn) instead of into /tmp/nacos/log/nacos-sdk.log. While Nacos is unreachable its reconnect messages, several a second, are replaced by three records: `nacos connection lost`, `nacos is still unreachable`, `nacos connection restored`

`registry_disabled: true` now means: run without Nacos. In addition to not registering, a configuration read with WatchConfig or `log_level_data_id` is the file `conf/nacos/<data id>`, and saving the file counts as a change
services on this version and on earlier ones keep finding each other
action: Nothing has to change. `nacos.log_dir` in your conf/*.yaml is ignored from now on and can be removed.
Only if your own code called nacosx.SharedNamingClient, NewNamingClient or NewConfigClient: use `nc, err := kitexx.Nacos(cfg.Config)` and then nc.Naming() or nc.ConfigClient().
To use the new configuration, see the section "Configuration that follows Nacos" in conf/README.md.

changes: devkit-common v0.3.4: `service.addr` takes a port. New services get `addr: 8888` in conf/dev.yaml and conf/prod.yaml instead of the quoted `":8888"`. A bare port listens on every network interface, exactly like `":8888"` did; `"host:port"` is still there for listening on one interface only
a bad `service.addr` is reported with the name of the setting and what it accepts, instead of "missing port in address"
action: Nothing has to change: `addr: ":8888"` in your conf/*.yaml keeps working. If you prefer the short form, replace the line with `addr: 8888` (your port) in conf/dev.yaml and conf/prod.yaml.

changes: devkit-common v0.3.3: log sampling says what it left out. Every second in which records were dropped ends with one record per level and message, "zlog: records dropped by sampling" with dropped_msg and dropped, so the size of a flood can be read from the log

conf/README.md has a new section on the three production safeguards of the logger (sampling, max_field_bytes, buffer): what each protects against, what it costs, and when to turn buffer on, which prod.yaml leaves off on purpose

the Docker image no longer contains conf/dev.yaml. A container whose APP_ENV got lost or overridden used to start with the development settings and look healthy: not registered in Nacos, so no caller found it, and logging colored text that a collector cannot parse. Now it refuses to start and names the configuration files there are
action:
Only if you run the image with APP_ENV=dev somewhere, for example in a development cluster: that no longer starts. Give that environment a file of its own:
cp conf/prod.yaml conf/test.yaml      # then adjust it, and deploy with APP_ENV=test
If you had edited the Dockerfile, the new one is next to it as Dockerfile.new; take over the two lines that mention /out/conf.

changes: devkit-common v0.3.2: the "logger configured" record of a starting service says where the values come from that the framework fills in: `service: order (from service.name)`, `env: prod (from APP_ENV)`, or `env: dev (APP_ENV is not set)`. In JSON these remarks, and which settings are defaults, are in "config_notes"

devkit-common v0.3.1: the first record of a starting service, "logger configured", lists the log settings in effect (level, format, stacktrace, sampling, buffer, max_field_bytes, service, env, version, host, output) under the names they have in conf/*.yaml, with "(default)" behind what was not set. It is written whatever the level
a typo in the log settings (for example format: consol) is now reported whatever the level; with level: error the warning used to filter itself out

devkit update no longer stops with an error from `go mod tidy` when a service still uses the log package that devkit-common v0.3.0 removed: it skips that step, says why, and goes on to show the steps below. 0.6.0 stopped before it could show them
action:
If your code still imports "<common>/log", move it to zlog, then finish the update by hand:
replace the import "<common>/log" with "<common>/zlog"
log.FromContext(ctx).Info("ping", "message", m)   ->   zlog.Ctx(ctx).Info("ping", zlog.Str("message", m))
go mod tidy && go build ./... && go vet ./...

changes: devkit-common v0.3.0: new logger zlog (on zap) replaces the log package. Console output for people: a color per level, file:line that GoLand and terminals turn into a link, key=value fields, stacks of errors and panics below the record with every frame a link. JSON output for collectors: service, env, host, version and the trace_id of the request on every record, never the same key twice
a trace_id follows a request from service to service (kitexx.ClientOptions now uses the TTHeader transport); zlog.Ctx(ctx) is the logger of the request
what Kitex and dependencies log (klog, log, log/slog) comes out in the same format
new log settings: format, stacktrace, max_field_bytes, sampling, buffer, version; log_level_data_id makes the level follow a Nacos configuration at run time
a service that cannot read its configuration now reports it through the logger; the Dockerfile sets ZLOG_FORMAT=json so that this line is JSON too
action:
The log package is gone from devkit-common, so handler code has to move to zlog. Replace the import "<common>/log" with "<common>/zlog" and rewrite the calls:
log.FromContext(ctx).Info("ping", "message", m)   ->   zlog.Ctx(ctx).Info("ping", zlog.Str("message", m))
slog.Error("save failed", "err", err)             ->   zlog.Error("save failed", zlog.Err(err))
Fields: zlog.Str, Int, Float, Bool, Dur, Time, Err, Any, Secret. go vet ./... finds what is left.
In conf/*.yaml replace `json: false` with `format: console` and `json: true` with `format: json`. The old key still works, so nothing breaks if you wait.
Clients made with kitexx.ClientOptions now speak TTHeader. Kitex servers accept it without any change; only a server that is not Kitex needs a look.

changes: devkit-common v0.2.1: when Nacos cannot be reached the service stops at once and names the address, the reason and the setting to check, instead of "client not connected, current status:STARTING" after a few seconds; it also explains a closed gRPC port (main port + 1000)
one Kitex version for the whole team: devkit update now also aligns the Kitex library in go.mod with the template, not only the generator version in the Makefile
make gen stops with a clear message when the installed kitex or thriftgo is not the team's version, instead of generating different code
versions can no longer be chosen per service or per project (needs devkit 0.1.9 or newer)
Dockerfile and GitLab CI use the Go release the common library needs (GoVersion, 1.26); with golang:1.24 the image refused to build because devkit-common requires Go 1.26
action:
If `make gen` now reports another kitex or thriftgo version, run:
make tools
If devkit.yaml has KitexVersion, ThriftgoVersion or CommonVersion under `vars:`, remove those lines; devkit 0.1.9 refuses them.

changes: library and tool versions (KitexVersion, ThriftgoVersion, CommonVersion) now follow the template on update instead of staying at the value from when the service was created; needs devkit 0.1.8 or newer
action:
Only if you want a service to stay on a specific version, pin it:
devkit update --set KitexVersion=v0.16.3

changes: new app/app.go, a file you own: the service's Config struct, a Setup function for its dependencies and shutdown cleanup, and optional extra server options
cmd/<service>/main.go is now pure framework code that calls app.Setup; nothing service-specific lives in it any more, so it can always be updated
action:
If you had edited cmd/<service>/main.go, it was left alone and the new version is next to it as main.go.new. Move your changes into app/app.go, then take the new file:
Config fields            -> the Config struct in app/app.go
kitexx.OnShutdown(...)   -> app.Setup
extra server options     -> app.ServerOptions
mv cmd/<service>/main.go.new cmd/<service>/main.go
If your handler needs dependencies, create them in app.Setup and pass them to handler.New(...).

changes: conf/README.md: a managed reference of every configuration setting, kept up to date by devkit update
new services get conf/dev.yaml and conf/prod.yaml with a detailed English/Chinese comment on every setting
action:
Your existing conf/*.yaml were not touched. For the explanations, read conf/README.md,
or create a scratch service with `devkit ngs` and copy the commented files from it.

changes: main.go: configuration is found from any start directory ($CONF_DIR, ./conf, next to the executable); start-up errors are plain messages instead of a panic
graceful stop: keeps serving after leaving Nacos, configurable drain time, kitexx.OnShutdown hooks that run after the last request
Kitex's internal logs use the same format as yours (logger=kitex); requires devkit-common v0.2.0, upgraded for you
action:
Optional, in each conf/<env>.yaml (defaults are 3s and 15s). Locally use deregister_wait: 0s so stopping is instant:
shutdown:
  deregister_wait: 3s
  drain_timeout: 15s

If the service owns resources, release them on shutdown. Since 0.4.0 this goes into app.Setup in app/app.go:
kitexx.OnShutdown("db", db.Close)

changes: the list of IDLs to generate moved from the Makefile to idl.mk, a file you own, so the Makefile can keep being updated
action:
If you had added IDLs to the IDLS line of the Makefile, put them into idl.mk:
IDLS := <service>/<service>.thrift other/other.thrift

changes: CI for GitLab (.gitlab-ci.yml) next to GitHub Actions; which one is generated follows where the code is hosted
action: If both files were generated and you only need one: devkit update --force --set CI=gitlab   (or github)
